t: Israeli Election Ends in Deadlock According to Exit Polls
s: Exit polls indicate a tie between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot. Voter turnout reached 77.7 per cent, with the Arab bloc projecting historic gains of up to 18 seats.

t: Local Ceasefire Holds in Ukrainian Town of Oleshky
s: A US-brokered local truce in Russian-occupied Oleshky took effect to deliver humanitarian relief and permit civilian evacuations. Both Russian and Ukrainian officials confirmed no violations were recorded during the initial hours.

t: Flávio Bolsonaro Flees Brazil for US Following Election Loss
s: Defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro fled to the United States after Brazil's Supreme Court ordered the surrender of his passports. The US State Department confirmed visas were issued to Bolsonaro and his family.

t: US Pentagon Iran War Costs Exceed $47 Billion as Houthis Strike Saudi Targets
s: Pentagon data revealed US military expenditure in the Iran war has exceeded $47 billion. Meanwhile, Yemen's Houthis launched ballistic missiles targeting Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery and defence ministry, calling Egyptian military support a declaration of war.

t: Togo deepens strategic and maritime ties with China
s: Togo is expanding its maritime ambitions and security coordination with Sahel states by strengthening strategic relations with Beijing. The partnership aims to position Lomé as a regional trade gateway to West Africa.

t: Singapore and Germany expand strategic partnership in AI
s: Singapore Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz agreed to step up industrial AI cooperation under an updated work plan. Both nations will also enhance research collaboration and foster ASEAN-EU ties.

t: Singapore and Indonesia create joint task force on haze
s: Singapore and Indonesia announced a joint task force to share intelligence and investigate companies linked to forest fires. Singapore is also planning legislative amendments to strengthen enforcement against transboundary haze polluters.

t: US Defence Secretary Hegseth heads to Philippines for ASEAN meeting
s: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth is visiting Cebu to meet Southeast Asian counterparts and regional allies ahead of the ASEAN Defence Ministers' Meeting. Discussions will focus on Indo-Pacific security and maritime cooperation.

t: North Korea deploys artillery and mobile guns along border
s: North Korea has stepped up military posture near the Demilitarised Zone by positioning coastal artillery and self-propelled guns. South Korea's defence ministry confirmed it is closely monitoring Pyongyang's move.

t: Japan considers testing long-range missiles at Indian firing ranges
s: Japan's Ground Self-Defense Force sent officials to India to evaluate using local test ranges for long-range missiles and small attack drones. The initiative aims to alleviate domestic training constraints in Japan.

t: Trump conditions acceptance of US midterm election results
s: US President Donald Trump announced while campaigning in Texas that he will accept upcoming midterm election results only if they are honest. The statement raised concerns over potential post-electoral challenges.

t: US selects Poland to host European Patriot PAC-3 maintenance hub
s: The US Department of Defence and Lockheed Martin selected Poland to host a new European maintenance and repair facility for Patriot PAC-3 interceptors. The hub will support allied Patriot operators across the continent.

t: Weibel to supply XENTA-M5 radars for Poland's counter-drone system
s: Danish radar manufacturer Weibel Scientific was selected to deliver XENTA-M5 3D radars for Poland's SAN counter-uncrewed aerial system programme. The radars will provide early detection and tracking of micro and mini drones.

t: France orders more SAMP/T NG systems with hypersonic capability
s: The French Ministry of the Armed Forces placed an order for additional SAMP/T NG air defence systems. The upgraded system incorporates Aster block 1NT missiles capable of intercepting hypersonic threats.

t: Lockheed Martin expands Alabama plant for ARRW production
s: Lockheed Martin announced an expansion of its Courtland, Alabama facility following a $694 million US Air Force contract for AGM-183A ARRW hypersonic missiles. The site will handle low-rate initial production for B-52 bomber integration.

t: Germany to procure Ukrainian BARS long-range missile-drones
s: The German Bundeswehr intends to acquire Ukraine's indigenously developed BARS long-range missile-drone system. The purchase aims to rapidly fill deep conventional strike capability gaps in the German armed forces.

t: Leaders of Finland and Norway speak directly with Putin on Ukraine
s: Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre held a joint telephone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The leaders stressed that European security hinges on resolving the war in Ukraine.

t: Jordan and Syria form joint security committee after air strikes
s: Following Jordanian air strikes against militant targets in southern Syria, both nations agreed to establish a joint security committee. The bilateral body will coordinate border security and manage cross-border incident repercussions.

t: Romania accuses Russia of grave security violation over sabotage plot
s: Romanian President condemned an alleged Russian sabotage operation targeting domestic critical infrastructure as a grave violation of a NATO member's security. Romanian authorities have heightened protection around key logistics hubs.

t: US intelligence confirms details of China's secret spaceplane
s: US intelligence agencies confirmed that China's reusable orbital spaceplane closely mirrors the design of the US Space Force's X-37B. The vessel continues to demonstrate extended autonomous operational capabilities in orbit.

t: US Space Force plans multivendor satellite constellation for GPS
s: The US Space Force issued requirements for a multi-provider satellite constellation to augment position, navigation, and timing capabilities. The initiative aims to build resiliency against signal jamming and anti-satellite threats.

t: US Army evaluates high-altitude balloons for Indo-Pacific ISR
s: The US Army is testing stratospheric high-altitude balloons to provide long-range sensing and targeting along the first island chain. The platforms offer low-cost, persistent surveillance in contested airspaces facing China.

t: Malaysia permits export of 700 tonnes of rare earths to US
s: Rare earth developer DTEC received approval to export up to 700 tonnes of raw rare-earth carbonate from Perak to the United States for research. The deal aligns with US efforts to diversify critical mineral supply chains.

t: SK Hynix announces $75bn shareholder return plan following strong Q3
s: South Korean memory chip maker SK Hynix reported a sevenfold increase in third-quarter profit, driven by global demand for AI memory chips. The company subsequently unveiled a $75 billion capital return plan for shareholders.

t: Helsing unveils Contra air defence system against mass drone strikes
s: German defence AI firm Helsing has launched its Contra air defence architecture, featuring two dedicated interceptors costing under $100,000 per shot. The system employs proprietary software to autonomously detect, track, and defeat saturating Shahed and Geran drone salvos.

t: US Air Force puts AGM-183A ARRW hypersonic missile into production
s: The US Air Force has reversed its near-cancellation of the AGM-183A Air-launched Rapid Response Weapon, officially ordering the standoff hypersonic missile into production. The weapon will arm B-52 and B-1 bombers to provide high-speed standoff strike capability.

t: Israel votes in general election amid reports of pre-poll Iran plans
s: Israelis headed to the polls on Tuesday in the country's first parliamentary election since October 2023. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu campaigned heavily on the Iranian threat following reports that he pushed military commanders for pre-election strikes on Tehran.

t: Egyptian parliament approves military deployment to defend Saudi Arabia
s: Egypt's House of Representatives voted on Monday to authorise military support to Saudi Arabia following a formal request by President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi. The deployment aims to shield the kingdom against escalating missile and drone attacks from Yemeni Houthis.

t: AUKUS designates USS Colorado as first rotational submarine for Australia
s: Defence chiefs from the US, UK, and Australia announced the Virginia-class fast-attack submarine USS Colorado as the first vessel assigned to Submarine Rotational Force-West. The deployment to HMAS Stirling operationalises Western Australia's continuous nuclear submarine presence under Pillar One.

t: Algeria deploys troops to Niger to protect border energy infrastructure
s: Algeria will deploy military personnel to the former French base at Madama in northern Niger to secure key energy facilities near the Libyan border. This marks the Algerian military's first foreign troop deployment since 1973.

t: Singapore revamps infantry battalions with tactical drone units and digital mapping
s: The Singapore Armed Forces is reorganising active infantry battalions, establishing two dedicated unmanned systems sections per company. Troops will employ micro-UAVs and networked battlefield maps to boost situational awareness and survivability in urban combat.

t: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz begins official visit to Singapore
s: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz arrives in Singapore on Tuesday for a two-day official visit, his first since taking office. Merz will hold bilateral talks with Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and deliver the 49th Singapore Lecture.

t: Indonesia affirms gas export reductions to Singapore meet contractual minimums
s: Energy Minister Bahlil Lahadalia confirmed cuts in natural gas exports to Singapore remain within contract limits of 91 to 92 per cent. Jakarta rejected criticism over resource nationalism, stressing domestic priority while pledging to honour legal commitments.

t: Malaysia set to receive initial pair of FA-50M light combat aircraft
s: The Royal Malaysian Air Force will take delivery of its first two FA-50M light combat aircraft from Korea Aerospace Industries on Friday. The aircraft form part of an 18-jet procurement intended to revitalise Malaysia's tactical fighter capabilities.

t: Flávio Bolsonaro seeks annulment of Brazilian presidential election result
s: Following Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's runoff victory, conservative challenger Flávio Bolsonaro refused to concede and filed to annul the election results, citing alleged irregularities. Federal police subsequently ordered Bolsonaro to surrender his passports as Brazilian financial markets tumbled.

t: Serbian opposition celebrates historic parliamentary victory over Vučić
s: Thousands gathered in Belgrade for a second night to celebrate the student-led coalition's parliamentary win over President Aleksandar Vučić's ruling party. The political transition raises questions regarding Serbia's future foreign policy and its traditional ties with Moscow.

t: Thailand fields Israeli Smart Shooter counter-drone sights on service rifles
s: The Royal Thai Army has begun equipping standard infantry rifles with Israeli-made Smart Shooter Smash fire-control optical systems. The computerised optics enable ground troops to accurately detect, track, and kinetically neutralise low-flying micro-UAVs.

t: Pentagon launches sprint programme for air defence uncrewed surface vessels
s: The US Department of Defense has initiated an accelerated acquisition sprint to develop and field production-ready maritime counter-drone surface vessels. The programme seeks autonomous boats equipped with air defence systems to protect fleet units from aerial swarm attacks.

t: India approves £20bn defence procurement including 300 K9 Vajra howitzers
s: India's Defence Acquisition Council has cleared procurement proposals valued at 2.12 lakh crore rupees (£20 billion). The approvals include acquiring 300 additional K9 Vajra tracked self-propelled artillery systems manufactured domestically in partnership with Hanwha.

t: Cyprus signs deal to acquire Israeli-equipped offshore patrol vessel
s: Cyprus signed a government-to-government agreement with Israel on Monday to acquire a new offshore patrol vessel. The ship will be fitted with advanced Israeli naval combat systems and sensors to bolster maritime surveillance in the eastern Mediterranean.

t: Russian ballistic missile strike damages Kyiv university before scheduled truce
s: Russian ballistic missiles struck a university campus and medical facilities in Kyiv on Monday, killing at least one person and injuring ten. The strike occurred days before a US-brokered humanitarian ceasefire is set to take effect in Oleshky.

t: Jordan strikes militant targets in Syria following deadly church shooting
s: The Royal Jordanian Air Force launched air strikes against militant hideouts in southern Syria after arresting three suspects linked to Friday's church attack in Karak that killed nine. Syria responded by closing border crossings with Jordan.

t: Mecca pact diplomats hold talks in Tehran to prevent regional escalation
s: High-level representatives from Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan met Iranian security officials in Tehran for emergency talks to avert all-out regional conflict. Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei welcomed the discussions, insisting regional security must exclude foreign intervention.

t: European E5 defence ministers pledge greater defence investments in Paris
s: Defence ministers of Germany, Britain, France, Italy, and Poland convened in Paris on Monday, publishing a joint call to accelerate European defence capabilities. The ministers reaffirmed commitment to NATO while stressing the necessity of self-reliant industrial and military capacity.

t: US intelligence warns China could deploy orbital directed-energy weapons by late 2020s
s: US intelligence agencies assessed that China may field operational directed-energy weapons in orbit before the decade ends. The space-based lasers or microwave systems could blind or destroy adversary optical and communications satellites in low Earth orbit.

t: US Navy to build hypersonic weapon support facility at Yorktown
s: Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command plans to construct a dedicated hypersonic missile facility at Naval Weapons Station Yorktown. The depot will handle, assemble, and store Conventional Prompt Strike hypersonic weapons for Zumwalt-class destroyers and Virginia-class submarines.

t: US denies South Korea requested exemption from advanced export controls
s: Washington has formally rejected South Korea's request for an exemption from expanded export controls on sensitive technologies. The decision prevents South Korean manufacturers from bypassing restrictions on supplying advanced equipment and semiconductors to constrained markets.

t: Lula secures historic fourth term in tight Brazilian election runoff
s: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won Brazil's presidential runoff with 51.8 per cent of the vote, narrowly defeating Senator Flávio Bolsonaro. The result halts a conservative shift in Latin America following a voting extension by the Supreme Court.

t: Serbian President Vučić concedes defeat to student protest coalition
s: President Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat in snap parliamentary elections after a student-led opposition movement secured a legislative majority. The result ends over a decade of dominance by Vučić following two years of widespread demonstrations.

t: Japan deploys domestic Type-25 long-range missile launcher in US drill
s: Japan deployed its indigenously produced Type-25 vehicle-mounted long-range missile launcher during a major joint exercise with US forces. The drill publicly demonstrated Tokyo's expanding counterstrike capabilities amid rising regional tensions.

t: US ballistic missile early warning fully restored to Ukraine
s: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that US early warning data for Russian ballistic missile strikes has fully resumed. The restoration follows high-level talks in Oslo with US special envoy Steve Witkoff.

t: Iranian military shoots down US drone over Bandar Abbas
s: The Iranian army announced that its air defences shot down an American drone over the southern port city of Bandar Abbas. The incident marks a sharp escalation as Washington and Tehran trade military threats across the Gulf.

t: Venezuelan opposition leader Machado returns home from exile
s: Opposition figure María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela after ten months in exile to press for a democratic transition. Her return follows national rallies and introduces fresh complications for Washington's regional strategy.

t: Singapore insists Indonesia honour natural gas supply contracts
s: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong affirmed that Singapore expects commercial gas contracts to be respected after Indonesia reduced pipeline exports. Wong stated that Singapore's gas importer will take all necessary measures to protect contractual rights.

t: China constructs three-kilometre airstrip on Antelope Reef
s: Satellite imagery reveals China has built a 3,000-metre runway on Antelope Reef in the Paracel Islands. The new facility significantly enhances Beijing's power projection and aerial reconnaissance reach across the disputed South China Sea.

t: Pyongyang claims September DMZ landmine blast was staged by Seoul
s: North Korea sent a letter to the UN Security Council alleging that an explosion injuring two South Korean soldiers on September 21 was fabricated. The accusation escalates cross-border tensions following recent clashes over border fortifications.

t: Marcos confirms new US-accessible military sites will be dispersed
s: President Ferdinand Marcos Jr stated that additional military sites accessible to US forces under defence cooperation agreements will be scattered across the Philippines. The dispersal strategy aims to strengthen archipelago defence against external threats.

t: Israel prepares for pivotal general election amid security lockdown
s: Israel will hold general elections on October 27 with polls indicating a close contest between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Gadi Eisenkot. Authorities announced full closures of West Bank crossings for voting day amid high tensions.

t: Saudi air defences intercept Houthi barrage as Riyadh airport reopens
s: Royal Saudi Air Defense intercepted a Houthi missile and drone barrage near Mecca. Simultaneously, commercial operations partially resumed at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh despite renewed strike threats from Yemen's Houthis.

t: EDGE integrates autonomous vessels and counter-drone systems in naval trial
s: The UAE's EDGE Group conducted a joint demonstration with the Emirati and US navies combining autonomous surface vessels with counter-drone capabilities. The trial tested integrated uncrewed systems against asymmetric aerial and maritime threats.

t: Kongsberg plans to offer Zone 5 strike missiles to Australia
s: Norway's Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace is preparing to market its Zone 5 strike missile to the Australian Defence Force. The company is actively exploring domestic production options to support sovereign manufacturing requirements.

t: Navantia launches seventh Avante corvette for Royal Saudi Naval Forces
s: Spanish shipbuilder Navantia launched the corvette Neom at its Bay of Cádiz shipyard, the seventh built for Saudi Arabia. The vessel is the second under a 2025 follow-on contract for multi-mission surface combatants.

t: Hanwha Ocean positioned as central partner in US naval shipyard renewal
s: US media highlighted South Korea's Hanwha Ocean as a pivotal partner in efforts to revitalize American naval shipbuilding. Expanding capacity remains critical for US naval sustainment despite high infrastructure costs and regulatory hurdles.

t: Zelenskyy announces trilateral Ukraine-Russia-US talks for November
s: President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that a trilateral meeting between Ukrainian, Russian, and US representatives will occur in November. Zelenskyy insisted that Western sanctions against Moscow must remain fully in place ahead of the negotiations.

t: SpaceX restricts Ukraine's military Starlink access over terms dispute
s: Elon Musk confirmed SpaceX restricted Ukrainian Starlink connections after alleging Kyiv used the satellite network for combat activities violating terms of service. Ukrainian officials denied breaching agreements as commercial connectivity was restored.

t: IDF chief reportedly clashes with Netanyahu over Iran strike orders
s: Israeli reports revealed an unprecedented confrontation in which the IDF Chief of Staff resisted directives from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu regarding operational action against Iran. Netanyahu dismissed the reports as baseless ahead of Tuesday's election.

t: France begins development of Standard 2 Falcon ARCHANGE SIGINT aircraft
s: The French Air and Space Force has begun developing the Standard 2 variant of its Falcon ARCHANGE electronic reconnaissance aircraft. The platform will provide advanced airborne signal intelligence capabilities following the retirement of Transall Gabriel aircraft.

t: South Korea records world's second-largest current account surplus
s: South Korea achieved the second-largest current account surplus globally, surpassing Germany and Japan on the back of surging semiconductor exports. Officials highlighted strong memory chip demand as the primary driver of national economic expansion.

t: Kim Jong-un visits China in first trip across new border bridge
s: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un visited Dandong, crossing a newly opened bridge over the Yalu River, state media confirmed on October 25. He met senior Chinese officials ahead of the Chinese Korean War entry anniversary.

t: Pentagon acknowledges US possesses weapons deployed in space
s: The US Secretary of the Air Force publicly acknowledged that Washington has deployed weapons in space. The rare admission ends decades of official strategic ambiguity surrounding American offensive and defensive space warfare capabilities.

t: Brazil votes in tightly contested presidential election runoff
s: Millions of Brazilians voted on October 25 in a knife-edge presidential runoff between incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Flávio Bolsonaro. Final opinion polls showed both candidates statistically tied following contentious economic debates.

t: Indonesia reduces natural gas pipeline exports to Singapore
s: Indonesia reduced natural gas pipeline exports to Singapore by roughly 9% to support domestic energy needs in Sumatra and Natuna. Singapore's Energy Market Authority confirmed the reduction affects under 2% of daily national demand.

t: Trump warns of potential Iran strikes as Tehran threatens Gulf routes
s: Donald Trump stated Washington is considering military strikes against Iran as early as Sunday unless diplomatic terms are met. Tehran vowed severe retaliation, barred US warships from the Persian Gulf, and prepared undersea cable contingency targets.

t: Singapore companies confirm compliance with transboundary haze notices
s: Six Singapore-registered companies confirmed they are complying with National Environment Agency notices issued under transboundary haze laws. Authorities requested corporate records to assess whether local entities contributed to Indonesian peatland fires.

t: Taiwan reports 21 of 24 US arms purchases on schedule
s: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense stated that 21 of 24 major US weapon procurement programmes are progressing as planned, with three facing delivery delays. Taipei continues working with Washington to accelerate delayed capabilities amid Chinese military pressure.

t: CCP reshuffles provincial leadership ahead of Beijing plenum
s: The Chinese Communist Party appointed new chiefs across six provinces on October 24 ahead of its Fifth Plenum meeting from October 26 to 29. The gathering is expected to review economic strategies and future leadership alignments.

t: Four Philippine Air Force pilots die in trainer plane crash
s: Two Philippine Air Force SF-260 trainer aircraft crashed during a formation training flight at Fernando Air Base on October 23, killing four pilots. The air force grounded remaining trainers pending an investigation into the collision.

t: Israeli raids displace over 1,200 in Hebron before election
s: Israeli security forces displaced more than 1,200 Palestinians in Hebron during operations launched after two soldiers were killed on Friday. Meanwhile, thousands rallied in Tel Aviv demanding a leadership change ahead of the October 27 election.

t: Serbia votes in early parliamentary elections following student rallies
s: Serbia held snap parliamentary elections on October 25 following two years of continuous student-led protests against the ruling coalition. The vote presents a direct challenge to the long-standing political dominance of President Aleksandar Vučić.

t: French carrier Charles de Gaulle tests HELMA-P counter-drone laser
s: The French Navy conducted operational trials of the CILAS HELMA-P laser weapon aboard the aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle under the L2AD programme. The system demonstrated close-in drone interception capabilities to enhance warship self-defence against aerial swarms.

t: USS Pinckney enters Phase Two modernization with SPY-6 radar
s: The USS Pinckney became the first Arleigh Burke-class destroyer to begin Phase Two of the DDG MOD 2.0 overhaul. The upgrade incorporates RTX's AN/SPY-6(V)1 radar to significantly bolster integrated air and missile defence against advanced threats.

t: Japan deploys RM40m counter-drone system to protect eastern Malaysia
s: Japan delivered a RM40 million counter-drone suite to Malaysia to safeguard airspace over Sepanggar naval base and Labuan. The system enhances detection and jamming capabilities against unauthorised unmanned aerial systems operating near strategic maritime facilities.

t: Lockheed Martin signs $218m deal with Karman for THAAD components
s: Lockheed Martin awarded a $218 million agreement to Karman Space & Defense to support expanded production of THAAD interceptors. Karman will supply critical composite and metallic components to help ramp up anti-ballistic missile manufacturing.

t: German defence ministry advocates fighter jet collaboration with Sweden
s: The German Ministry of Defence called for exploring joint development of a next-generation combat aircraft with Sweden. The proposal follows growing German defence industry pushback against continued participation in the Franco-German NGF programme.

t: Ukraine restores Starlink connectivity as US operational requests revealed
s: Ukrainian military forces confirmed Starlink satellite communications returned to normal operation after recent network throttling. Concurrently, reports revealed that US administrations have repeatedly asked SpaceX to alter service coverage in Ukraine and the Middle East.

t: Saudi air defences intercept Houthi ballistic missiles targeting Riyadh
s: Saudi air defences intercepted three Houthi ballistic missiles launched towards Riyadh, Taif, and Yanbu on October 24. Concurrently, Houthi strikes hit targets in Aden, including the airport and a coastguard base, prompting retaliatory Saudi airstrikes.

t: French Army selected to field future long-range ballistic missiles
s: France's armed forces ministry confirmed the French Army will operate future land-based deep-strike ballistic missiles being developed under the Military Programming Law. Studies launching in 2026 will design sovereign systems capable of striking targets beyond 1,000 kilometres.

t: US Marines trial autonomous drone swarms for air defence drills in Hawaii
s: The US Marine Corps conducted live-fire training in Hawaii using autonomous drone swarm technology developed by Australian firm Boresight. The trials evaluated ground-based air defence responses and counter-swarm tactics against coordinated unmanned threats.

t: Beijing urges US to drop proposed curbs on outbound tech investment
s: China called on Washington to abandon proposed restrictions limiting American outbound investment in advanced technologies like artificial intelligence and semiconductors. Beijing warned the measures would disrupt global supply chains and multilateral commerce.

t: US Army activates dedicated air and missile defence battalion in Guam
s: The US Army has activated an air and missile defence battalion on Guam to strengthen defences against Chinese and North Korean threats. The unit integrates THAAD batteries as part of Washington's layered regional architecture.

t: South Korea proposes military talks with North Korea on border demarcation
s: Seoul has proposed bilateral military talks with Pyongyang to clarify the Military Demarcation Line and restore direct communication hotlines. The offer follows escalating tensions and recent landmine detonations along the demilitarised zone.

t: Russia and Ukraine agree to humanitarian ceasefire in Oleshky
s: Moscow and Kyiv have agreed to a localized humanitarian ceasefire in the occupied town of Oleshky starting on October 29. The White House announced the US-brokered truce to allow emergency aid deliveries and civilian evacuations.

t: Israel locks down West Bank following deadly shooting near Hebron
s: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered a full lockdown across the occupied West Bank after Palestinian gunmen killed two soldiers near Hebron. Sweeping military operations were launched just four days before Israel's general election.

t: Singapore serves legal notices to 10 companies over transboundary haze
s: The National Environment Agency issued legal notices to 10 Singapore-based firms, including Asia Pulp & Paper, under transboundary haze laws. Singapore will also establish an expert panel to assist cross-border investigations.

t: Philippine defence chief warns towing Sierra Madre would be an act of war
s: Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro warned that any Chinese attempt to forcibly tow the grounded BRP Sierra Madre would constitute an act of war. Manila affirmed it will vigorously defend its sovereign rights and personnel.

t: Japan approves bill restricting foreign land purchases near military bases
s: The Japanese cabinet approved a bill requiring prior government approval for land purchases surrounding Self-Defense Forces bases. The law specifically restricts foreign government-linked acquisitions due to concerns over espionage and drone launches.

t: Sarawak state assembly set to dissolve ahead of elections
s: Sarawak's state legislative assembly will dissolve on October 26, triggering state elections within 60 days. The ruling GPS coalition is widely favoured to retain power amid broader political pressure on Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim.

t: US Justice Department sues to delay Alaska Senate election certification
s: The US Department of Justice filed a lawsuit seeking to block certification of Alaska's Senate election results if the Republican incumbent loses. Critics and Democrats condemned the move as an unprecedented federal intervention.

t: Singapore Army tests mobile C-UAS as Air Force seeks helicopter defences
s: The Singapore Army conducted operational trials of a mobile counter-drone capability to safeguard field units. Meanwhile, the Republic of Singapore Air Force is seeking dedicated counter-UAS protection systems for its helicopter fleet.

t: US Army funds L3Harris long-range drone interceptor development
s: The US Army awarded funding to L3Harris to develop and flight-test a long-range drone interceptor. The effort seeks to provide cost-effective surface-to-air options against hostile uncrewed aerial systems.

t: Spanish Navy and Navantia design IAMD-dedicated F110 frigate variant
s: Navantia and the Spanish Navy are designing an air defence evolution of the Bonifaz-class F110 frigate. The variant will feature advanced integrated air and missile defence capabilities against complex aerial threats.

t: General Atomics partners with Spirit Defense on FQ-42 CCA drone ramp-up
s: General Atomics partnered with Spirit Defense to expand manufacturing capacity for the USAF FQ-42 Collaborative Combat Aircraft. The initiative supports surging demand for autonomous uncrewed fighter wingmen over the next six years.

t: Indian Navy issues tender for four landing platform docks
s: The Indian Navy issued a request for proposals to procure four landing platform docks. The acquisition programme aims to significantly bolster expeditionary amphibious warfare and regional power projection capabilities.

t: Cargo vessel sinks off Romania following suspected Russian drone strike
s: A commercial cargo vessel sank off Romania's Black Sea coast following an alleged Russian drone strike, leaving one sailor dead and three missing. Romanian authorities condemned the strike near NATO waters.

t: Gunmen kill seven at church funeral in Jordan
s: Masked gunmen opened fire during a funeral at a church in Karak, killing seven people and wounding 34. Security forces launched an extensive manhunt as King Abdullah II vowed retaliation.

t: Study indicates Saudi missile plant expansion may produce advanced weapons
s: Satellite imagery indicates Saudi Arabia is expanding a domestic missile manufacturing facility, possibly with Chinese assistance. The site may produce more capable ballistic missiles, enhancing deterrence against regional threats.

t: France and Britain conduct first joint airborne nuclear strike exercise
s: The French Air and Space Force and the Royal Air Force conducted Exercise Rummy, marking their first joint airborne nuclear strike exercise. The drill operationalises bilateral nuclear cooperation agreements signed in 2025.

t: Russian military satellite shadows US spacecraft linked to Ukraine
s: Washington accused Moscow of deliberately manoeuvring a Russian military satellite into close proximity with a US-registered commercial satellite supporting Ukraine. The incident raises alarms over escalating orbital counter-space activities.

t: US military bans BYD electric vehicles from Japanese air base
s: The US military barred BYD electric vehicles from entering an air base in Japan over national security and surveillance concerns. The decision highlights growing allied scrutiny over connected Chinese vehicles near sensitive defence infrastructure.

t: First Russian diesel cargo heads to US under Trump-Putin agreement
s: A tanker carrying the first shipment of Russian diesel bound for New York has departed following a deal between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin. The delivery bypasses broader Western restrictions on Russian petroleum products.

t: Russia bombards Kyiv after indicating readiness for peace talks
s: Russian forces launched three waves of ballistic missiles and drones against Kyiv hours after Moscow agreed to resume US-brokered talks. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strikes proved there is no real change in the Kremlin's stance.

t: Pentagon and Lockheed Martin agree decade-long deal for 850 F-35s
s: The US Department of Defense and Lockheed Martin reached a 10-year framework agreement securing at least 850 F-35 fighters. The procurement remains subject to annual congressional budget approvals.

t: Aramco evacuates Dhahran base as deadly Houthi strikes hit Saudi Arabia
s: Saudi Aramco instructed staff to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters following repeated Houthi missile and drone strikes. Interceptions and impacts across eastern Saudi Arabia left at least two people dead and struck King Fahd International Airport.

t: Magnitude 7.0 earthquake strikes northern Tibet, killing at least 16
s: A powerful magnitude 7.0 earthquake struck Nagqu in northern Tibet late on October 22, destroying hundreds of homes. Chinese authorities confirmed at least 16 people died and more than 30 were injured.

t: European Parliament awards Sakharov Prize to US-sanctioned ICC
s: The European Parliament awarded its Sakharov human rights prize to the International Criminal Court. The symbolic move comes shortly after the Trump administration imposed financial sanctions against the tribunal's judges.

t: Indonesian Air Force tests fighter jet dispersal landings on toll road
s: The Indonesian Air Force conducted touch-and-go landing trials with four combat aircraft on the Pasuruan-Probolinggo toll road in East Java. The drill tested operational readiness and alternative landing strips during wartime contingencies.

t: North Korea readies border loudspeakers as Seoul appeals to UN
s: Kim Yo-jong warned that North Korean border propaganda loudspeakers will be operational within days in response to South Korean actions. Seoul called for de-escalation and prepared a formal complaint to the UN Security Council.

t: Singapore expands mask distribution as air quality temporarily improves
s: Singapore authorities began a second round of mask distribution, expanding eligibility to seniors aged 60 and above. Air quality improved to moderate levels after 18 consecutive days of haze caused by Indonesian peat fires.

t: Lula and Bolsonaro in dead heat ahead of Brazil presidential runoff
s: Opinion polls show President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flavio Bolsonaro tied ahead of Sunday's runoff election. The campaign has seen sharp polarisation over evangelical influence and allegations of social media bias.

t: Malaysian court stays deregistration of opposition coalition Perikatan Nasional
s: The Kuala Lumpur High Court granted an interim stay against the Registrar of Societies' deregistration of Perikatan Nasional. The ruling allows the main opposition bloc to continue political operations and contest upcoming state elections.

t: South Korean counter-drone laser achieves 100% intercept rate in Army drill
s: South Korea's indigenously developed anti-drone laser weapon system achieved a 100 per cent intercept success rate during operational Army live-fire trials. Hanwha-built systems are now positioned for potential export to European and Middle Eastern customers.

t: China's KJ-3000 radar jets enter serial production at Shaanxi facility
s: Satellite imagery confirmed four new KJ-3000 airborne early warning and control aircraft outside a Chinese production facility. The radar aircraft represents the primary next-generation platform to replace China's legacy KJ-200 and KJ-500 AEW&C fleets.

t: Pentagon launches 120-day sprint to field counter-drone armed USVs
s: The US Defense Innovation Unit launched a 120-day rapid acquisition effort for uncrewed surface vessels armed with counter-drone capabilities. The initiative aims to protect naval surface task groups against swarms of cheap one-way attack drones.

t: Denmark procures Kongsberg and Covenant long-range strike missiles
s: The Danish Ministry of Defence decided to acquire long-range strike missiles from Norway's Kongsberg and British developer Covenant. Copenhagen aims to establish an offensive standoff deterrent to respond to potential peer adversary strikes.

t: US Missile Defense Agency awards $75m contract to Long Wall
s: The Missile Defense Agency awarded a $75 million contract to start-up Long Wall to test low-cost midcourse interceptors. The project seeks scalable, economical intercept options to counter large ballistic missile salvos.

t: Ukraine cleared to buy military equipment directly through NATO agency
s: Ukraine secured access to procure arms and ammunition directly via the NATO Support and Procurement Agency. The mechanism provides Kyiv with an alternative supply channel amid growing uncertainty over direct bilateral US military aid.

t: US and Israel draft Iran strike plans as Tehran warns Gulf shipping
s: US and Israeli officials are reportedly preparing contingencies for renewed military strikes on Iranian infrastructure following upcoming elections. Concurrently, Iran's IRGC claimed to have hit seven vessels and threatened Gulf energy transit routes.

t: UK parliamentary report warns of severe Royal Navy Arctic ASW gaps
s: A British parliamentary committee warned that the Royal Navy faces acute anti-submarine warfare shortfalls in the High North. The inquiry cautioned that depleted surface escort numbers leave critical subsea infrastructure vulnerable to Russian sabotage.

t: US Space Force launches 'Spider' programme to revamp GPS ground ops
s: The US Space Force initiated a new ground modernisation effort dubbed Spider to overhaul GPS operations. The programme aims to introduce open-architecture software and enhance cyber resilience against peer jamming and spoofing threats.

t: Palantir insists allied military AI platform has no remote kill switch
s: Palantir affirmed that its software deployed across NATO headquarters contains no vendor-controlled kill switch. The assurance follows European concerns over technological dependence on US providers after recent commercial satellite service restrictions.

t: TSMC seeks non-Chinese rare-earth alternatives for chipmaking tools
s: TSMC has begun auditing suppliers and seeking non-Chinese motor alternatives to reduce reliance on Beijing-controlled rare earths. The initiative seeks to insulate advanced semiconductor fabrication lines against Chinese export restrictions on critical permanent magnets.

t: Russia and Ukraine open to US-brokered talks
s: Moscow and Kyiv have signaled a willingness to resume trilateral peace talks following meetings between US envoy Steve Witkoff and Vladimir Putin. However, heavy missile strikes hit Kyiv concurrently as skepticism remains high.

t: US orders staff evacuation from Saudi Arabia
s: The US State Department ordered non-essential embassy personnel and families to leave Saudi Arabia. The move comes as sustained Houthi drone and missile strikes target the kingdom's infrastructure.

t: North Korea prepares border loudspeakers
s: North Korean leader's sister Kim Yo-jong inspected border fortifications and warned that propaganda loudspeakers directed at South Korea will be operational within days. Seoul vowed an overwhelming response to any provocations.

t: Meta fined $25 billion over data privacy
s: A US court ordered Meta to pay a record $25 billion penalty following a jury verdict finding the company lied to users about data access during the Cambridge Analytica scandal.

t: Global satellite services revenues projected to surge
s: A new industry report forecasts that global satellite connectivity and services revenues will expand by 44% to reach $145 billion by 2035.

t: Singapore and UAE launch economic partnership talks
s: Prime Minister Lawrence Wong and UAE President Sheikh Mohamed Zayed Al Nahyan witnessed the signing of energy, water, and disease vector control agreements in Abu Dhabi. Both nations also agreed to start formal economic partnership negotiations.

t: Prabowo hits back at MSCI over stock market downgrade threat
s: Indonesian President Prabowo accused MSCI of trying to intimidate Indonesia after a warning of a potential market downgrade triggered a sharp equities sell-off. Jakarta rejected allegations linking the market rout to state investors.

t: Malaysia bans Waze for civil servants over security concerns
s: Malaysia has barred civil servants from using the Waze navigation app, citing data security links to Israel. Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim recommended switching to the domestic alternative Tuju.

t: Japan recovers wreckage of crashed Global Hawk drone
s: The Japan Air Self-Defense Force retrieved a six-metre section of the fuselage belonging to a crashed RQ-4 Global Hawk drone. An ongoing investigation follows a series of recent parts-drop incidents across military bases.

t: Meta sued in Australian class action over harm to children
s: A class action lawsuit has been filed in Australia against Meta on behalf of eight plaintiffs alleging social media platforms cause intentional harm to children.

t: Israeli voters head to polls amid regional tensions
s: Israeli military personnel have begun voting ahead of the upcoming national parliamentary elections. Key candidates and Arab minority lists are mobilizing voters as prime ministerial contenders clash over security strategy.

t: France orders additional SAMP/T NG air defence systems
s: The French DGA has ordered additional SAMP/T NG Franco-Italian medium-range ground-based air defence systems. The procurement accelerates the delivery schedule outlined in the current military programming law.

t: US Navy spots AIM-174B and AIM-260 missiles on Super Hornet
s: A US Navy F/A-18 Super Hornet was photographed carrying both the AIM-174B and the secretive AIM-260 JATM long-range missiles. The dual loadout marks a significant milestone for naval aviation strike capabilities.

t: Iran defence minister vows advanced air defence technologies
s: Iran's new defence minister pledged to upgrade the country's national air defence network using new technologies. The move comes amid rising regional threats and active posturing by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

t: US Air Force outlines 1,509 combat-ready fighter jet target
s: The US Air Force informed Congress that it requires 1,500-plus combat-coded fighter jets by 2035. F-35s are projected to make up 40 percent of the fleet, with F-47s ultimately replacing F-22s.

t: Qatar, Turkey, Pakistan and Indonesia sign Badr defence pact
s: Representatives from Qatar, Turkey, Pakistan, and Indonesia have signed the Badr defence cooperation memorandum of understanding. The agreement aims to deepen multilateral defence industrial ties and joint military cooperation.

t: India's BEL signs ₹770-crore radar contract
s: India's Ministry of Defence has signed a ₹770-crore contract with Bharat Electronics Limited for low-level tactical radars. The procurement aims to boost the military's low-altitude airspace surveillance network.

t: German military warns of significant Russian sabotage threat
s: A classified internal analysis by the German military warns of a high risk of Russian sabotage targeting domestic infrastructure and military installations. Authorities have raised the internal sabotage threat level accordingly.

t: AI vulnerabilities trigger global security scramble
s: Developers rushed to release emergency patches after autonomous AI tools uncovered critical security flaws in PHP. The programming language powers over 70% of websites worldwide.

t: UK deploys Typhoons for Saudi air defence against Houthis
s: The UK will deploy Typhoon fighter jets and an A400M transport aircraft to Saudi Arabia to conduct defensive air missions against Houthi missile and drone strikes. Military advisers will also support Saudi staff officers.

t: US resumes strike warnings to Ukraine amid new diplomatic push
s: Washington has resumed sharing intelligence and advance strike warnings with Kyiv following talks between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy and US envoys in Norway. US envoy Steve Witkoff is now set to meet Vladimir Putin in Moscow.

t: NATO reinforces Black Sea air patrols after Russian drone strikes
s: NATO announced the deployment of additional maritime patrol aircraft and drones to the Black Sea region to protect commercial shipping. The move follows recent drone strikes off the coasts of Bulgaria and Romania attributed to Russia.

t: North Korea threatens border escalations as Seoul vows firm response
s: Pyongyang has threatened to restart loudspeaker broadcasts and deploy additional tactical strike weapons along the Military Demarcation Line. South Korea's military ordered a firm response to any North Korean border provocations.

t: Singapore air quality moderates as Indonesia battles forest fires
s: Air quality in Singapore showed slight improvement while remaining in the moderate-to-unhealthy range due to Indonesian forest fires. Indonesia declined foreign assistance, stating domestic resources are managing the fires.

t: Malaysia de-registers main opposition coalition before elections
s: Malaysian authorities have officially de-registered the main opposition coalition Perikatan Nasional ahead of upcoming national elections. The decision prevents constituent parties from contesting ballots under a unified alliance banner.

t: Chinese naval tonnage output more than double US volume
s: A report released ahead of Euronaval reveals China built more than twice the naval tonnage of the United States between 2024 and 2025. The expansion further narrows the naval fleet gap in the Indo-Pacific.

t: South Korea recalls Kyiv embassy staff following POW dispute
s: Seoul is withdrawing additional diplomatic personnel from its embassy in Ukraine following a dispute over Kyiv's public disclosure of captured North Korean soldiers. Relations between the two nations have cooled significantly.

t: Romania appoints pro-European government ending five-month crisis
s: Romania's parliament voted in a new pro-European government led by independent Prime Minister Luca Niculescu. The appointment resolves a five-month political crisis following three previously failed attempts to form a cabinet.

t: Alberta rejects proposal for independence referendum
s: Voters in Alberta decisively rejected a proposal to hold a referendum on leaving Canada, delivering a major setback to the province's separatist movement. Separatist leaders vowed to continue campaigning despite the clear defeat.

t: Japan and Malaysia sign RM40m counter-drone deal
s: Malaysia and Japan have signed a 40 million ringgit contract to provide counter-drone systems to the Royal Malaysian Navy. The agreement enhances maritime surveillance and C-UAS capabilities in Southeast Asia.

t: US Air Force pilot controls uncrewed combat aircraft in flight
s: An active-duty F-22 Raptor pilot successfully controlled an uncrewed FQ-44 Collaborative Combat Aircraft in flight. The test highlights progress in manned-unmanned teaming capabilities for air superiority missions.

t: Starlink slowdown hampers Ukrainian air defences
s: SpaceX founder Elon Musk reportedly instructed Starlink to throttle satellite communications over Ukraine, hampering Ukrainian aerial defence operations. Ukrainian arms manufacturers are now actively seeking alternative satellite networks.

t: Indian Navy contracts $68m BrahMos retrofit for legacy warships
s: India's Ministry of Defence signed a 68 million dollar contract to equip legacy Kashin-class destroyers and Veer-class corvettes with BrahMos supersonic cruise missiles. The upgrade extends the firepower of the surface fleet.

t: US Navy expands Gecko Robotics maintenance contract to $300m
s: The US Navy extended its AI-driven predictive maintenance contract with Gecko Robotics to 300 million dollars. The firm uses wall-climbing robots and drones to inspect hull integrity and structural welds on naval ships.

t: Canada and Turkey draft defence and energy cooperation pact
s: Canada and Turkey plan to sign a joint declaration during Mark Carney's visit to Ankara to deepen bilateral cooperation across four sectors, including defence and energy. The agreement reinforces ties between the NATO allies.

t: Shabwa missile attack death toll rises to 73 in Yemen
s: The death toll from a Houthi ballistic missile attack on a pro-government military training camp in Shabwa governorate has risen to 73 recruits. The strike represents one of the deadliest single attacks in months.

t: US Navy controls MQ-25A drone via satellite across 2,100 miles
s: Aircraft carrier USS Ronald Reagan remotely operated an MQ-25A Stingray uncrewed tanker in Illinois while underway in the Pacific. The test was conducted over a proliferation Low Earth Orbit (pLEO) satellite network.

t: South Korea outlines 2031 military satellite launch on Nuri rocket
s: South Korea announced plans to launch its first dedicated military satellite aboard its indigenous Nuri space launch vehicle in 2031. The mission forms part of Seoul's sovereign space reconnaissance roadmap.

t: Trump administration delays Patriot interceptor deliveries to Ukraine
s: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy accused Washington of withholding paid-for Patriot interceptors and restricting strike warnings. The hold-up leaves Ukrainian cities exposed as European allies reportedly await US approval to transfer their own stocks.

t: Saudi Arabia postpones flagship summit as Houthi strike kills over fifty
s: Riyadh has postponed its 2026 Future Investment Initiative to 2027 and directed civil servants to work remotely following Houthi attacks. A separate Houthi ballistic missile strike on a Yemeni military camp in Shabwa killed at least 53 recruits.

t: Russian satellite executes unprecedented shadowing of ICEYE radar spacecraft
s: Russia's Kosmos 2612 satellite carried out extensive manoeuvres to approach within metres of ICEYE X36, a commercial radar-imaging satellite linked to Ukrainian operations. Western defence officials highlighted the incident as an acute demonstration of counter-space proximity operations.

t: Australian lawmaker Helen Haines critically injured in deliberate vehicle attack
s: Independent federal MP Helen Haines remains in critical condition after a vehicle deliberately struck her outside her constituency office in Victoria. Police arrested a 43-year-old male driver at the scene following civilian intervention.

t: France imposes night curfews in Paris and major cities after violent riots
s: French authorities ordered overnight curfews in Paris, Marseille and six other municipalities following days of rioting, looting and student demonstrations. Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez acknowledged police temporarily lost control in several urban sectors.

t: Trump floats trilateral nuclear summit with Xi and Putin
s: US President Donald Trump stated he is open to holding a three-way summit with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping next month to address nuclear arms control. The prospective meeting could coincide with next month's APEC summit in China.

t: Singapore extends transboundary haze notices to ten Indonesian firms
s: Singapore issued legal notices to three additional Indonesian firms under the Transboundary Haze Pollution Act, bringing the total to ten. Senior Minister K Shanmugam warned the Republic will deploy every regulatory and economic lever against errant companies.

t: Singapore and Qatar commit to upgrade ties to strategic partnership
s: Singapore and Qatar renewed an energy pact to deepen liquefied natural gas cooperation and agreed to work towards a formal strategic partnership. The upgraded framework will encompass expanded collaboration across defence, trade, investment and energy security.

t: Manila summons Chinese envoy over armed conflict remarks
s: The Philippines summoned China's ambassador after he publicly claimed Beijing would easily win any war between the two countries. Manila denounced the rhetoric as an unacceptable threat to national sovereignty amid ongoing maritime tensions.

t: Hegseth visits Netanyahu in Tel Aviv ahead of parliamentary election
s: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in an unannounced visit ahead of Israel's closely contested election on October 27. The meeting followed Donald Trump's public endorsement forecasting Netanyahu's victory.

t: Fortem and MBDA partner to integrate European counter-drone defences
s: Fortem Technologies and MBDA have formed a partnership to integrate counter-unmanned aircraft systems across European defence frameworks. The initiative combines Fortem's airspace security radars and interceptors with MBDA's command-and-control and air defence systems.

t: Germany drops rapid procurement plan for Boeing MQ-28 Ghost Bat
s: Berlin has scrapped its fast-track acquisition plan for Boeing's MQ-28 Ghost Bat collaborative combat aircraft. The German Air Force will instead launch a broader competitive tender for loyal wingman systems that will run into the 2030s.

t: Pentagon signs framework for 25,000 APKWS precision rocket kits annually
s: The US Department of Defense signed an agreement with BAE Systems for up to 25,000 Advanced Precision Kill Weapon System guidance kits per year. The framework guarantees high-rate production capacity to convert unguided 70mm rockets into laser-guided munitions.

t: Rheinmetall and MSC acquire Romanian Mangalia shipyard for €138m
s: Rheinmetall and shipping group MSC agreed to purchase Romania's Mangalia shipyard for €138 million to establish a Black Sea naval hub. The site will support dual-use production and maintenance for commercial vessels and naval warships.

t: Ukraine conducts first front-line medical evacuation using uncrewed aircraft
s: The Ukrainian military announced the world's first front-line evacuation of a wounded combatant using a heavy-lift uncrewed aerial vehicle. The drone lifted the soldier from a heavily mined kill zone inaccessible to ground extraction teams.

t: Egyptian parliament postpones vote on military mandate for Saudi defence
s: Egypt's parliament adjourned a session scheduled to authorise potential armed forces deployments to assist Saudi Arabia against Houthi strikes. Opposition parties urged members to abstain, citing ambiguity over Cairo's exact military commitments and operational scope.

t: NATO allies assemble in Bucharest to counter Russian hybrid warfare
s: NATO member states and partner nations convened in Bucharest for a dedicated symposium on countering Russian hybrid threats, critical infrastructure sabotage and cyberattacks. Senior commanders stressed that the alliance must accelerate procedural adaptations to deter aggression.

t: Japan launches MMX mission to explore Martian moons
s: Japan successfully launched its Martian Moons eXploration probe on a five-year mission to Phobos and Deimos. The spacecraft aims to achieve the first landing and sample return from Phobos to investigate solar system origins.

t: US Navy installs CPS hypersonic weapon system on destroyer Lyndon B. Johnson
s: Huntington Ingalls Industries confirmed that Zumwalt-class destroyer USS Lyndon B. Johnson is receiving the Conventional Prompt Strike hypersonic missile system. The US Navy awarded a sea-trials contract to validate the weapon's integration.

t: US sanctions five Chinese entities over stolen AI trade secrets
s: The US Department of Commerce sanctioned five Chinese entities tied to an ex-Google engineer accused of stealing proprietary artificial intelligence source code. Washington alleged the stolen technologies were transferred to advance Chinese civilian and military AI developments.

t: Australia launches tender for army medium-range air defence
s: The Australian Department of Defence has formally released a tender for a medium-range ground-based air defence solution for the Australian Army. The programme aims to rectify a recognised critical gap in national air defence.
w: Crucial export opening for medium-range surface-to-air missile suppliers looking to expand in the Indo-Pacific theatre.

t: Kyiv hit by ballistic missile barrage amid intelligence friction with Washington
s: Russia launched heavy ballistic missile and drone strikes against Ukrainian energy sites across eleven regions overnight. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy noted initial early-warning gaps from partners before confirming US intelligence sharing had been unblocked.
w: Underlines allied reliance on US early-warning sensor architecture against rapid ballistic threats.

t: US and Japan begin record Keen Sword 26 military exercise
s: The United States and Japan have commenced exercise Keen Sword 26, deploying 57,000 personnel across Japanese territory until 29 October. The manoeuvres include live deployments of long-range surface-to-ship missiles and remote island defence scenarios.

t: Singapore threatens legal action against Indonesian firms over toxic haze
s: Singapore warned errant companies linked to Indonesian forest fires that it will deploy every legal and regulatory lever available. The National Environment Agency issued statutory notices to three further firms, bringing the total targeted to ten.
w: Heightened regulatory pressure may affect regional industrial operations and cross-border commercial ties.

t: Macron rejects interior minister's resignation following violent French riots
s: French President Emmanuel Macron has declined the resignation of Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez following widespread weekend rioting over living costs. The government has instructed police to adopt new tactics, while curfews are under consideration.

t: Australia integrates strike drones and sea mines onto Ghost Shark XL-UUV
s: Australia has unveiled payload integration for its Ghost Shark extra-large autonomous submarine, including aerial drone swarms and sea mines. The platform is designed to conduct long-range missions in tandem with crewed naval assets.
w: Signals the operational shift towards autonomous undersea strike swarms in Western Pacific maritime denial.

t: Second Chinese uncrewed submarine mothership spotted in Guangzhou
s: Satellite imagery shows Guangzhou Shipyard International has built a second mothership designed to deploy and recover large uncrewed underwater vehicles. The vessel represents a scaled-down variant of an earlier prototype.

t: Singapore and Sweden agree to expand emerging technology partnership
s: Institutions from Singapore and Sweden will broaden bilateral cooperation covering next-generation positioning technologies and sustainable energy. The initiative deepens technical and research collaboration between both defence and industrial ecosystems.

t: Trump endorses Netanyahu as Israeli legislative campaign enters final week
s: Donald Trump has endorsed Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ahead of Israel's closely fought parliamentary election on 27 October. The campaign has been marked by deep divisions over Iran policy and widespread artificial intelligence-generated deepfakes.

t: Lula and Bolsonaro clash in volatile debate ahead of Brazilian run-off
s: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and challenger Flávio Bolsonaro traded fierce accusations during a televised debate ahead of the 25 October run-off. Recent opinion polls indicate the gap between both candidates has tightened.

t: Romanian F-16s shoot down two drones in NATO airspace over Black Sea
s: Romanian Air Force F-16 fighters intercepted and downed two suspected Russian drones over Romanian territorial waters. The incident follows repeated allied airspace alerts near the Black Sea corridor.

t: Airbus links German and Swedish air defence units into NATO shield
s: Airbus has successfully integrated German and Swedish air defence assets into a unified command-and-control framework under NATO IAMD initiatives. The link enables rapid multinational sensor-to-shooter coordination.
w: Demonstrates growing demand for interoperable multinational C2 architectures within European and allied air defence.

t: Jeumont Electric selected for Polish A26 submarine propulsion suites
s: French company Jeumont Electric will supply three complete low-signature electric propulsion systems for Poland's A26 submarines under the Orka programme. The contract advances Poland's naval fleet renewal.

t: Denmark procures additional Naval Strike Missiles from Norway
s: Denmark has concluded a government-to-government agreement with Norway to acquire extra Kongsberg Naval Strike Missiles. The anti-ship missiles will upgrade the Royal Danish Navy's frigate fleet.

t: Ukrainian long-range drones strike Saint Petersburg oil refinery
s: A Ukrainian one-way attack drone strike ignited a major fire at an oil refinery in Saint Petersburg overnight. The attack forms part of sustained efforts targeting Russian rear fuel and logistics infrastructure.

t: Houthi missile strike kills 18 in Yemen as Egypt signals support for Riyadh
s: A Houthi ballistic missile strike hit a Yemeni government military training camp in Shabwa governorate, killing at least 18 personnel. In response, Egypt stated its readiness to provide Saudi Arabia necessary military backing.

t: Sweden outlines 2027 NATO ground and Patriot air defence deployments
s: Stockholm has detailed planned 2027 military deployments, committing ground forces to NATO forward presences in Finland and Latvia. Sweden also confirmed it will continue operating Patriot surface-to-air missile batteries in Poland.

t: US Air Force acknowledges operational weapons deployed in space
s: The Secretary of the US Air Force has publicly confirmed that the United States maintains operational weapons in space. The disclosure marks an unusual departure from traditional strategic ambiguity regarding orbital military systems.
w: Confirms space as an active operational domain, accelerating demand for space domain awareness and tracking.

t: Anduril explores European production for Steelfin interceptor missiles
s: US defence technology firm Anduril is considering establishing European manufacturing facilities for its newly revealed Steelfin interceptors. The move seeks to address rapid European demand for ground-based air defence and counter-drone munitions.
w: Intensifies competition for European and allied GBAD and counter-air interceptor procurement contracts.

t: China imposes export controls on tunnel-boring machines citing national security
s: China's Ministry of Commerce has implemented export restrictions on advanced tunnel-boring machines. The measure is expected to constrain infrastructure and border-tunnel projects sought by India.
